sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168][F1][F10].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [D161][F5][D200][F6][D238][F7].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion and has grown only 1.8% and 4.9% in the two years since [D274][F8][D308][D342][F10].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue and contributed just 0.1pp of the 4.9% growth, while natural gas added 4.4pp on 37.4% growth [D551][D553][D342][D586][D585].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in 2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, inclusive of Marathon Oil volumes, and higher realized gas prices of $824 million [P28].
Lower 48 contributed 8.0pp of FY2025 revenue growth on 11.8% growth, and the segment was 70.2% of revenue [D713][D712][D711].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 against 4.9% revenue growth, and basic EPS fell 18.7% as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D343][D342][D344][D356].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% in FY2025, faster than the 4.9% revenue growth [D352][D342].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
DD&A rose $1.9 billion in 2025, primarily due to the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
Production and operating expenses rose $1.6 billion in 2025, again primarily from Marathon Oil plus $216 million of restructuring severance [P24].
The 36.9% effective tax rate in FY2025 was above the 32.4% of FY2024, and net margin fell 3.3pp from the prior year [D332][D298][D351].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.07x window median [F59][D333][D855].
The 2025 decline from $20.1 billion in 2024 resulted from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by operations from the 2024 Marathon Oil acquisition [P6].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median, but the pack stops reporting free cash flow after FY2022 [D833][D834][F73].
Capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 and 1.35x D&A, the highest capital-intensity reading in the window [D222][D228].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion at FY2025, up 13.4%, against $1.0 billion of current debt [D335][D357][X203].
Net cash was -$12.9 billion, or -67.0% of revenue, in FY2020, the last year the pack can compute it before the debt reporting break [D155][D156].
In 2025 the company spent $12.6 billion on capital, $5.0 billion on buybacks, $4.0 billion on dividends and $0.9 billion to retire debt, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Return on average equity was 12.4% in FY2025, below the 14.9% energy peer median and in the 33rd percentile of six peers [D341][D853][D852].
Revenue in the table is a later recast for every year: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons that span the recast mix two presentations, so the 9.1% CAGR should be read with that caveat [F168].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2020, so net cash and debt growth cannot be computed for FY2021 onward [F157].
The balance-sheet read for the latest five years rests on cash and current debt alone, which understates gross leverage.
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 as realized commodity prices declined across all products [D274][P40].
That decline was price-driven rather than volume-driven, so it is cyclical rather than a structural loss of share.
Whether net margin holds above the 15.4% FY2025 level or falls toward the 17.9% median, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D831].
Whether operating cash flow stays above the $19.8 billion FY2025 level or slips toward the $20.0 billion FY2023 figure, in the FY2026 10-K [F59][F57].
Whether the diluted share count keeps rising from 1,253.4 million in FY2025, reversing the 2.1% decline of FY2024, in the FY2026 10-K [X131][D322].
